source.title: The dynorphin/kappa opioid system as a modulator of stress-induced and pro-addictive behaviors

confidence_rationale: Establishes that the dynorphin/kappa-opioid (KOR) system mediates the DYSPHORIC/aversive component of stress -- functionally dissociable from mu-opioid reward -- giving Q-075 a receptor-level handle for the commitment-threshold kappa/mu opioid overlay. Discounted because (a) the paper says nothing about COMMITMENT or commitment-entropy -- that mapping is a large REE-specific interpretive leap, and (b) it emphasises tight CRF-KOR COUPLING, which entangles the putative commitment axis with the stress/harm axis rather than showing it as independent.
failure_signatures: KOR/dynorphin is repeatedly shown to be downstream of and co-activated with CRF stress signalling; if the commitment-threshold axis is grounded in a receptor system that is mechanistically fused to the stress/harm system, the axes may co-vary rather than dissociate -- the exact collapse Q-075 warns against.
The paper's construct is dysphoria/aversion and pro-addictive relapse, not commitment threshold or commitment entropy; the REE translation may be grounding the wrong behavioural variable in KOR.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Activation of the dynorphin/kappa-opioid-receptor (KOR) system mediates the aversive, dysphoric component of stress and potentiates drug-seeking and stress-induced reinstatement; it does so in concert with CRF, and its aversive signature is separable from the rewarding (mu-opioid) actions of abused drugs.
mapping.ree_translation: Q-075 predicts the commitment-threshold axis maps to a kappa/mu opioid commitment-entropy overlay. This paper grounds the kappa side: KOR is a distinct, selectively-targetable receptor system carrying an aversive/dysphoric signal dissociable from mu-opioid reward -- the kind of receptor-level separability the axis-grounding hypothesis needs, and a candidate substrate for a commitment-cost / aversive-threshold signal.
mapping.mapping_caveat: OUT-OF-DOMAIN by design (V3 has no opioid receptor subtypes; receptor rung is out_of_domain per receptor_subtype_intervention_layer.md Section 4). The translation from 'KOR mediates dysphoria/aversion' to 'kappa/mu governs a commitment-threshold / commitment-entropy overlay' is a substantial interpretive leap the paper does not make. The heavy CRF-KOR coupling documented here actively threatens the dissociation Q-075 wants, because it fuses the commitment candidate to the stress/harm system.
mapping.source_context: Mechanistic review of rodent behavioural pharmacology and signal transduction (conditioned place aversion, stress-induced reinstatement, CRF-dynorphin cascades).

confidence_components.notes: Strong, well-cited mechanistic review (source_quality 0.75). mapping_fidelity is low because the commitment-threshold mapping is unsupported by the paper and the CRF-KOR coupling cuts against clean dissociation; rodent + out-of-domain transfer keeps transfer_risk at 0.50.
